mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with UNRATE rising > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during three-month periods of INDPRO > 0.5% monthly decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases volatility and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a strengthening residential construction sector, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during five consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 50,000 for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during three consecutive months with PAYEMS < 50,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 6-month moving averages signals broad-based demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and INDPRO exceed their 6-month moving averages.
